statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band after an orderly two-way Friday close, while Stress stays elevated on a post-crisis-high long end and an unresolved Middle East energy sequence.
recommendation: Tail remains below the WATCH threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow danger window covers the post-close futures hour into the 21:00 UTC CME weekly settlement; the remainder of the published window is a weekend halt in which no continuous NQ price path exists.
headline: Orderly two-way Nasdaq-100 close into the weekend halt, with Stress elevated on a 5.18% long end and an unresolved Hormuz sequence
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,608.14 (+0.42%) inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range, about 59 points below its session high, and December NQ futures trade near 30,889 (+0.40%) after fading a 30,997.25 high within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range. Neither extreme was held into the close, retracements printed through the afternoon, and VIX fell 5.04% to 14.88 from a 15.94 high, so the persistent no-retracement structure that defines Tail is absent. The broader tape confirmed the same two-way resolution: the S&P 500 closed +0.51% at 7,743.41, the Dow +0.93% at 51,828.62 and the Nasdaq Composite +0.48% at 27,068.72, all three notching weekly gains despite the bond move. The macro backdrop nonetheless remains genuinely difficult. The 10-year Treasury yield settled at 5.18% after an intraday 5.23% and a sixth consecutive weekly rise, with the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47% on the latest H.15 release; reporting cites resilient private-sector data, energy-driven inflation and hawkish central-bank commentary, and notes a 5.501% 30-year intraday peak described as the highest since June 2004. WTI eased 1.89% to 92.82 and settled near 92.41, with Brent near 104.32, after Iran's foreign minister proposed a conditional seven-day sequence to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, contingent on a ceasefire including Lebanon, the lifting of the naval blockade, oil-sanction waivers and release of frozen assets; Washington has not answered. Final September Michigan sentiment at 48.1 was a four-month low with five-year inflation expectations at 3.4%. Shared Finviz context was partial this cycle, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; the available latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings were internally dispersed rather than uniformly aligned and are treated as delayed supporting context only, never as live NQ structure. That combination keeps Stress elevated and Tail low. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekly settlement halts continuous price discovery for the remainder of the published window, so the forecast path describes a dormant market with decaying evidence freshness rather than an improving regime.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Tail stayed inside a 17-22 band and Stress inside 54-59, with the mapped state oscillating between EA_ON and WATCH. The overnight Asian and European hours were the calmest stretch, Tail peaked at 22 during the 09:00 and 11:00 UTC European trend-up phases, and the US session resolved back toward the low band from 15:00 UTC onward as retracements returned and volatility decayed. No assessment was published for the 13:00 UTC clock-hour, which is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The current hour covers the post-cash-close futures window into the 21:00 UTC CME weekly settlement, after which the published path describes a full weekend halt with no continuous NQ price discovery through the end of the window. Tail steps down to a structural weekend floor and lifts only fractionally late on Saturday as conditional proximity to the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen builds; that step is an allowance for gap risk, not observed structure. Confidence decays steadily through the halt because live price-path evidence stops refreshing, and Stress stays in the elevated band because the post-crisis-high long end, the unresolved Hormuz conditions and next week's core PCE, ISM and payrolls calendar all remain in force.
